query: How should we design a concise clinical metadata template to capture population, diagnosis, intervention type/dose, outcomes, and study design?

response.query: How should we design a concise clinical metadata template to capture population, diagnosis, intervention type/dose, outcomes, and study design?
response.answer: Design a concise clinical metadata template with fields for population demographics, diagnosis, intervention details, outcomes, and study design. Use standardized codes for consistency. Keep it simple and focused on essential data.

results.content: 240 - 248 1836-9553 (ISSN); 1836-9561 (ISSN) Publication Date: 2023-10-01 Publisher DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jphys.2023.08.006 Downloaded from http://hdl.handle.net/1959.4/unsworks_84635 in https:// unsworks.unsw.edu.au on 2026-05-15 Research The smallest worthwhile effect on pain intensity of nonsteroidal anti-inﬂammatory drugs and exercise therapy for acute and chronic low back pain: a beneﬁt-harm trade-off study Harrison J Hansford a,b, Matthew D Jones a,b, Aidan G Cashin a,b, Raymond WJG Ostelo c,d, Alessandro Chiarotto e, Sam A Williams b, Saurab Sharma a,b, Jack J Devonshire b, Michael C Ferraro a,b, Michael A Wewege a,b, James H McAuley a,b a School of Health Sciences, University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia; b Centre for Pain IMPACT, Neuroscience Research Australia, Sydney, Australia; c Department of Health Sciences, Faculty of Science and Amsterdam Movement Science Research Institute, Vrije Universiteit, Amsterdam, The Netherlands; d Department of Epidemiology and Data Science, Amsterdam University Medical Centre, Vrije Universiteit, Amsterdam, The Netherlands; e Department of General Practice, Erasmus MC, University Medical Centre, Rotterdam, The Netherlands K E Y W O R D S Clinical importance Patient-reported outcome measures Smallest worthwhile effect Low back pain Exercise A B S T R A C T Question: What are the smallest worthwhile effects of nonsteroidal anti-inﬂammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for people with acute and chronic low back pain (LBP)? For acute LBP, the smallest worthwhile effect of NSAIDs additional to no intervention was a 30% (IQR 10 to 40%) reduction in pain intensity.
